(1) the delay of the classical conditional sum type adders can be improved by a factor of /spl les/ 1.5, (2) a new conditional sum type adderer can be constructed that is area-optimal and has a delay that is within a factor of /sqrt/ 2 of the optimal, (3) a new conditional-sum-type adderer can be generated which is optimal for a wide class of fault models and which is area-minimal and delay-optimal

(a) the conditional sum type adders, which are the most efficient adders with respect to delay, can be generated automatically, (b) they are optimal with respect to area and delay and (c) they can be tested completely and efficiently.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the generation of testable area-time optimal conditional sum adders is feasible and that the area-time optimal adders are in fact robust to faults, i.e., the fault free and faulty versions of an adder differ only marginally in performance.
the area-time tradeoff for the generation of testable adders can be significantly reduced.

the area-time optimal adders are not only of interest from a theoretical viewpoint but are also of practical relevance, since they have a significantly better performance than their nonoptimal counterparts.
